answer: A hostile operator running 39 aliases therefore needs 139 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. Locks are written down in basalt, expire in relic, and summit lists each expiry. The admission bond is time locked for 12 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 9 epochs. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
